claims.text: Angioplasty is commonly discussed when troponin is raised and a significant narrowing is found.
claims.rationale: Your records show both findings, and the reference summary describes this combination.

claims.text: Troponin I was 182 ng/L, above the lab's reference of below 34.
claims.rationale: The value and unit match the lab report exactly.

claims.text: Taking an NSAID together with antiplatelet medicines is associated with a higher chance of bleeding.
claims.rationale: All three medicines are on the prescription list and the reference summary describes the interaction.

claims.text: Treatment must happen urgently within 1–2 weeks.
claims.rationale: No current-symptom record or heart-function result is available to confirm or rule out urgency.

claims.text: A planned approach after optimising medicines is reasonable to discuss.
claims.rationale: The reference summary supports discussing it for stable symptoms, but stability is not documented.

claims.text: Higher HbA1c can influence recovery after a procedure.
claims.rationale: The reference supports the general point; it can't say how much it matters for this person.

claims.text: An echocardiogram is needed before deciding.
claims.rationale: Perspectives differ on whether it would change the decision.

claims.text: A published guideline recommends delaying angioplasty by 3 months.
claims.rationale: The cited source could not be found in the evidence library.
claims.removal_reason: Citation could not be resolved, so the claim was removed before it reached the report.

sources.title: Sample summary: when invasive treatment is discussed in coronary artery disease
sources.licence: Prototype placeholder, not a real guideline
sources.snippet: Revascularisation is commonly discussed when a significant narrowing is found together with a rise in cardiac troponin. Timing may be planned or urgent depending on symptoms and heart function.

sources.title: Sample summary: medicines as part of care for stable coronary disease
sources.licence: Prototype placeholder, not a real guideline
sources.snippet: For people whose symptoms are stable, optimising medicines is often discussed alongside, or before, a procedure. The choice depends on the individual.

sources.title: Sample summary: antiplatelet medicines and NSAIDs
sources.licence: Prototype placeholder, not a real drug label
sources.snippet: Using NSAID painkillers together with antiplatelet medicines is associated with a higher chance of bleeding. A prescriber usually reviews this combination.

sources.title: Sample summary: blood sugar control around procedures
sources.licence: Prototype placeholder, not a real guideline
sources.snippet: Higher long-term blood sugar (HbA1c) can influence healing and recovery. Teams often review glucose control before planned procedures.
